basis: Corticospinal disease; spastic bladder in 80-99% reflects neurogenic dysfunction without established direct urinary tract injury.

decisions.renal: none: frequent spastic bladder reflects impaired neural control; direct urinary tract damage is not established.

basis: Brachydactyly and cerebellar dysfunction define the syndrome; nystagmus does not establish intrinsic eye damage. Strabismus frequency is unspecified.

decisions.ocular: none: defining nystagmus is consistent with cerebellar ocular motor dysfunction; intrinsic ocular damage or common independent visual impairment is not established.

basis: Filariae occupy skin and subcutis, causing nodules and chronic dermatitis; damaging ocular involvement is geographically variable and not established at >=30% overall.

decisions.ocular: none: ocular inflammation can cause permanent damage, but its frequency is not established at >=30% across this infection umbrella.

basis: Schwann-cell neoplasm; GI wall occupation occurs in roughly half of early reported cases. Subcutaneous involvement is insufficiently quantified.

decisions.gastrointestinal: involved: roughly half of early reported tumors occupy gastrointestinal submucosa, meeting the threshold for direct organ occupation.

basis: Skeletal dysplasia and contractures define the syndrome; mild intellectual disability accompanied the sole reported family of three affected siblings.

decisions.neurologic: involved: mild intellectual disability accompanies the reported three-sibling phenotype; it is associated rather than a defining skeletal feature.

basis: Nephrocalcinosis, hearing loss and joint contractures each occur in 30-79%. Frequent GI malformations and ocular abnormalities are omitted under the four-axis cap.

decisions.gastrointestinal: none: cleft palate and annular pancreas occur in 30-79%, but are omitted under the cap in favor of renal damage, hearing loss and multiple joint contractures.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: multiple joint contractures and skeletal malformations occur in 30-79%, supporting persistent locomotor impairment.

basis: Collecting-duct cysts and congenital hepatic fibrosis define ARPKD; hepatic fibrosis occurs in 80-99%, pulmonary hypoplasia in 30-79%.

decisions.hepatic: primary: congenital hepatic fibrosis and ductal plate abnormalities are defining components of ARPKD; fibrosis occurs in 80-99%.

basis: Frontal sinus mucosal inflammation belongs to pulmonary; the umbrella includes acute and chronic disease without a required infectious or immune-mediated cause.

decisions.infectious_immune: none: inflammation alone does not establish infection, autoimmunity or another defined immune-mediated mechanism across this umbrella.

basis: Mitochondrial myopathy with weakness and elevated CK in 4/4; learning disability in 4/4 supports neurologic involvement. Respiratory insufficiency reflects muscle dysfunction.

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: pervasive myopathy defines the supplied phenotype, with proximal/axial weakness, elevated CK and Achilles contractures in 4/4 patients.

basis: Locally aggressive adipocytic tumor typically arising in deep extremity soft tissue; superficial synonyms do not establish predominantly subcutaneous disease.

decisions.dermatologic: none: subcutaneous variants occur, but this unrestricted concept does not establish common skin or subcutaneous involvement.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: atypical lipomatous tumor typically originates in deep extremity soft tissue associated with the locomotor system.
